sender.en: A new online friend or match, often after a “wrong number” text

name.en: Romance and crypto “coaching”: a new friend teaches you to invest

how.en: Someone you meet on a dating app, social media or through a “wrong number” text builds a friendship or romance over weeks. They move the chat to a private app, say they make money trading crypto, and offer to coach you. They guide you to a trading website or app that shows big profits, and may let you withdraw a little at first. When you try to take your money out, you are asked for taxes or fees, and then they disappear.

text.en: A stranger contacts you, often by a “wrong number” text or on a dating app, and becomes friendly.
They move the conversation to WhatsApp or another private app and talk about love or friendship.
They say they earn a lot trading crypto and offer to coach you.
They guide you to a trading platform and push you to deposit more and more.
Hi, is this Linda? We were supposed to meet for coffee… Oh sorry, wrong number! You seem nice though. Where in Canada are you?
My uncle is an analyst and I follow his crypto signals. Yesterday I made 30%. I can show you how, just open an account on this platform: [link]

met online and he taught me crypto

trading platform won't let me withdraw

showed me how to make money with crypto
open an account on a trading platform
Someone you haven’t met in person professes love or close friendship quickly.
They move the chat to a private app and avoid meeting or video calls.
They offer to coach you on crypto or show you their profits.
The platform shows big gains but asks for taxes or fees before a withdrawal.
Don’t reply to “wrong number” texts from strangers.
Never invest on a platform suggested by someone you only know online.
Never send money or crypto to someone you haven’t met.
Report it to your local police and the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre, and call your bank if you sent money.
